bullets.title: GOOGL: Q2 Cloud +82% YoY, but negative FCF and capex raise trigger PT cuts
bullets.body: Alphabet Q2 revenue $119.80B beat consensus; Cloud revenue $24.77B grew 82% YoY with 35.6-36% operating margin and $514B backlog. However, FY26 capex raised 8% to $195-205B, FY27 capex flagged as significant step-up, and quarterly FCF turned negative (-$5.86B) for the first time in company history. Sell-side 88% Buy with average PT $434 (27% upside), but JPM cut to $420, Truist to $420, DA Davidson to $350 neutral; Freedom Broker upgraded to Buy at $400 PT; Wedbush added to Best Ideas list.

bullets.title: TSLA: Q2 operating margin hits 7-year low of 1.4%; stock -6-8% on cash burn, SBC concerns
bullets.body: Tesla Q2 gross margin fell from 21.1% in Q1 to 16.8% in Q2, with operating margin at a 7-year low of 1.4%. Stock-based compensation of $1.15B nearly equaled total non-GAAP shareholder earnings of $1.153B, and the stock trades at 90x LTM EBITDA. MS cut PT to $400 from $417 citing worsening cash burn; Hedgeye flagged 'Do NOT Buy' into earnings; Piper maintains OW citing FSD subscription growth (200k net q/q paid user increase, 1.5M total subs).

bullets.title: NOW: Strong Q2 beat — cRPO +21.5%, AI ACV >$1B, stock +5-6%
bullets.body: ServiceNow Q2 subscription revenue grew 23% YoY cc (150bps above high-end guidance), cRPO grew 21.5% YoY cc (200bps above guidance), and operating margin 29.5% came in 300bps above guidance. AI ACV exceeded $1B including Moveworks; management targets AI at 30% of total ACV by 2030. Sell-side 90% Buy, avg PT raised +1% to $140.65 (47% upside); FY26 subscription revenue guidance raised to $15.76-15.78B.

bullets.title: TXN: Q2 beat with data center +100% YoY; GS maintains Sell, Citi raises PT to $345
bullets.body: Texas Instruments Q2 EPS $2.14 beat $1.94 consensus; revenue $5.46B beat $5.26B; Q3 guided to $5.65-6.15B (+4.8% above consensus). Data center grew +20% sequentially and doubled YoY; automotive strength driven by China EV/hybrid demand; gross margin 61.4% beat by 180bps. Goldman raised PT to $225 but maintains Sell on GM headwind concerns; Citi raised PT to $345 (Buy); KeyBanc raised to $400 (OW). Sell-side 47% Buy, 45% Hold, 8% Sell with avg PT $320.

bullets.title: TMUS: Q2 EPS $2.99 beats by 40c, FCF guidance raised; but Q3 guide light, stock -8%
bullets.body: T-Mobile Q2 EPS $2.99 vs $2.59 estimate; EBITDA $9.54B beat $9.38B; FCF guidance raised to $18.4-18.8B. However Q3 postpaid net adds guided ~250K (below Street) and service revenue ~$19.3B below expectations, driving the stock -8%. Morgan Stanley maintains Overweight; underlying EBITDA growth decelerating to +8.9% in H2 ex-M&A. No material AI traffic surge observed yet; FWA capacity remains ample with 15M subscriber target by 2030 intact.

bullets.title: AT&T: Wolfe upgrades to Outperform, $29 PT (26% upside) on improving churn and 11% EPS CAGR
bullets.body: Wolfe Research upgrades AT&T from Peer Perform to Outperform with $29 PT, citing 2Q postpaid phone churn improving to 0.86% y/y despite a price increase and converged fiber-mobile strategy gaining traction. Projects 11% adj. EPS CAGR and 16% annual total returns, not reflected in near-trough valuation. Starlink threat viewed as multi-year away from materializing.

bullets.title: CMCSA: Q2 beats on Peacock profitability and wireless; Theme Parks soft
bullets.body: Comcast Q2 adjusted EPS $1.04 vs $0.97 estimate; wireless net adds 448K vs 384K estimate (surpassing 10M total lines). Peacock achieved first-ever quarterly profit at $189M EBITDA (vs -$101M YoY), revenue $1.90B beat $1.76B. Theme Parks Orlando remains soft through Q3. Separation targeted for mid-2027; buybacks paused through process. Free cash flow $4.60B beat $3.57B estimate.

bullets.title: MU/Memory: MS recommends buying the dip; DRAM cycle inflection risk flagged by Artisan
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley recommends buying the dip in memory stocks (MU, WDC, SNDK). Separately, Artisan's David Samra warns that 85% DRAM gross margins are attracting simultaneous capacity additions from Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron, and Chinese state-subsidized producers, making current valuations difficult to justify at above-historical-peak implied margins. ChangXin Memory Technologies IPO (July 27, $8.5B raise) adds competitive pressure.

bullets.title: HUT/RIOT: Morgan Stanley initiates both Overweight as powered-shell AI/crypto plays
bullets.body: MS Stephen Byrd initiates HUT (OW, $263 PT, 141% upside) and RIOT (OW, $36 PT, 68% upside) as crypto/data-center powered shell providers. HUT generated ~$17-18.50/watt shareholder value in recent transactions vs. peers trading at $2-4/watt; RIOT expected to land deal at Corsicana (1GW) or Rockdale (635MW available). APLD initiated Equal-weight at $36.50 PT (21% upside).

bullets.title: GEV: Morgan Stanley raises PT to $1,350 on strong demand visibility
bullets.body: MS raises GE Vernova PT to $1,350 from $1,250, viewing the recent -9% pullback as overdone given strong demand signals and 5-year visibility into the power equipment cycle. Analyst sees Brent +5% and oil/energy rally as a constructive backdrop for the stock.

bullets.title: RDDT: DA Davidson rates Buy on unique first-party data moat; DOMO acquisition adds $125M EBITDA
bullets.body: DA Davidson rates RDDT Buy, citing unique first-party data as competitive moat. RDDT is purchasing most of DOMO's assets for $355M (1.1x CY26 revenue) with potential $90M expense synergies and $125M EBITDA accretion. GOOGL partnership pays $60M/yr (renewal expected 1H27); June YoY web traffic decelerated but Q2 DAU growth in-line to modestly ahead of consensus.

bullets.title: SNAP: Specs tech solid but margins pressured; activist pushing $500M cost save via shutdown/spinoff
bullets.body: DA Davidson notes SNAP Specs viewed positively by developers, positioned as wearable computer vs META's AI glasses. However, Specs segment pressures profitability and activist is pushing for spin-off or shutdown of the unit which could save ~$500M annually. SNAP also nearing settlement of youth addiction litigation; META is the sole remaining defendant.

bullets.title: SEI: Morgan Stanley upgrades to Top Pick, raises PT to $125 (27% upside) on AI-driven margin expansion
bullets.body: SEI beat 2Q26 EPS by $0.22, driven by both revenue and expense strength; 4 consecutive quarters of pre-tax margin expansion and 3 consecutive quarters of record EPS. MS cites AI as a driver of results (not a disintermediator) and raises PT to $125 representing 27% upside. Named MS's SMID-cap Top Pick.

bullets.title: PLTR: Citi expects US commercial reacceleration with +140% YoY growth; cuts PT to $200
bullets.body: Citi expects Palantir US Commercial to reaccelerate after 1Q deceleration, with intra-quarter checks positive and potential $800M+ net adds in USC RDV. Analyst raises estimates but cuts PT to $200 on multiple compression. PLTR reports next week.

bullets.title: WING: DA Davidson maintains Buy, lowers 2Q SSS to -6% but sees 2H rebound; trades at all-time low 19x EV/EBITDA
bullets.body: DA Davidson lowers WING 2Q26 SSS estimate to -6% (from -4%) on continued pressure from younger/lower-income customers, but expects 2H return to positive LSD-MSD SSS driven by loyalty program, Smart Kitchen, and flavor innovation. Stock down 42% YTD and -20% in July, trading at all-time low 19x EV/EBITDA. Club Wingstop loyalty pilot drove 7% frequency increase and 30% higher avg ticket. PT $200.

bullets.title: MSFT preview: Azure ~41% growth expected; Copilot needs 6M+ net seat adds; FY27 capex ~$250B
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley maintains Overweight on MSFT ahead of earnings (Jul 29). Azure expected ~41% cc growth (1pt beat vs guide); paid Copilot seats at 20M need 6M+ net adds for upside. FY27 capex modeled at $250B (vs Street $233B), with quarterly capex reaching high-60s in F2H27. MS views MSFT as the clearest enterprise AI inflection play.

bullets.title: AMZN: Bezos pushing Prime Video AI redesign; Alexa redesigned to reduce Anthropic reliance
bullets.body: Jeff Bezos is directing Prime Video to make AI central to a service overhaul (project 'Lighthouse'), featuring AI-driven recommendations. Separately, Amazon has redesigned Alexa to rely less on Anthropic's AI models as it builds more internal AI capability. AMZN -3% in pre-market on Republican Senate inquiry over Chinese marketplace influence.

bullets.title: HUBS: Citi cuts PT to $217 on GTM transition headwinds; caution on sales cycles
bullets.body: Citi cuts HUBS PT from $230 to $217 ahead of earnings, citing GTM transition headwinds, sales cycle extension, and partner performance concerns. Contrast with NOW's strong beat and raised guide suggests enterprise software bifurcation between AI-native platforms and traditional CRM/marketing tools.

bullets.title: NVDA: Chinese open-source AI models reinforce GPU dominance; UAE to import high-end AI chips
bullets.body: Analysis notes that proliferation of Chinese open-source AI models (trained on NVIDIA GPUs) reinforces NVDA's dominance rather than undermining it. Separately, UAE announced plans to import high-end AI chips from the US 'very soon,' opening a potential new demand channel. GOOGL's expanded capex and hyperscaler survey median 2027 capex of ~$1.1T supports continued AI infrastructure spending.

bullets.title: Macro: 10yr yield at 4.69% year-high; oil WTI >$90, Brent near $100 on Houthi tanker attacks
bullets.body: US 10-year yields hit a year-to-date high of 4.69% (technical target 4.8%) and 2-year at 4.32%, driven by strong jobless claims (187K, lowest since 1969), oil spike, and anticipated bond supply. WTI crude surpassed $90/bbl (+4.8%) and Brent approached $100 on Houthi attacks on Saudi tankers in the Red Sea. July Fed rate hike odds rose to 38%; analysts flag 4.7% 10yr yield and $100 oil as risk-off triggers for equities—particularly growth/tech.
